settings.text: You have a team of designers and developers, and you need a full PLM: assortment planning, time and action calendars, costing, and a portal for many suppliers.
You want AI image generation for concepts, colourways and on-model renders.
You need an API, custom integrations or role-based permissions across several brands.
You want to see the price before you talk to sales, and try it free without a demo.
You need the pack to come with drawn flats, graded measurements and a pattern checked to sew, not only a place to keep them.
You want one partner from the idea to finished goods: samples, production and the factory, handled.

settings.us: A design studio (the Design Lab) and a manufacturer. The Lab makes the pack; Future Basics samples and produces it.
settings.them: A fashion PLM (plans: Core, Pro, Enterprise) and a separate AI design product. Its site describes working with your suppliers through a vendor portal, not making the product itself.

settings.us: Design Lab $499 for 90 days, or membership $100 a month. Your first tech pack is free, and the Make page gives a tech pack PDF of any piece you build there, no sign-up.
settings.them: PLM prices are not published: every plan says to book a demo. AI Design: Design Starter $35 and Design Pro $75 per user per month, billed yearly; Enterprise on request.

settings.us: Build a piece on the Make page and download its tech pack, free, no sign-up.
settings.them: No free trial is stated on its pricing pages.

settings.us: Drawn for you from 382 professional flat sketches across 24 garment styles, front and back, measured in inches.
settings.them: The AI design tool turns sketches into "clean flat images or on-model renders". The PLM lists an Adobe Illustrator plug-in.

settings.us: Drafted from the measurements, and checked: every seam is walked to make sure the pieces sew together.
settings.them: Not mentioned on the pages we read.

settings.us: Open the Lab and start from the recipe menu, a sketch, a photo or your own tech pack PDF.
settings.them: Core lists 2-week onboarding. The home page claims 10-day data migration and implementation, including moving old Excel and PDF tech packs.

settings.us: Future Basics makes it. Factories also get a link to the pack in their language, with messages on the pack.
settings.them: A vendor portal, with several factories assigned to one tech pack and their communication kept apart.

settings.us: You can describe a piece in words to start it, or build it from the menu. Flats and patterns are drawn, not generated.
settings.them: AI design from a text prompt, a sketch or an inspiration photo, with colourway variations, mood boards and visual line plans.

settings.heading: future basics or onbrand?
settings.lede: Onbrand is a PLM for fashion teams, with an AI design tool sold on its own. Future Basics is a design studio and a manufacturer: the Design Lab draws the flats, grades the measurements and checks the pattern sews, and then we make the product.
